verdict.rationale: Antigravity documents running multiple agents in parallel, and Git worktree support lets those agents work in isolated folders. That covers the parallel-execution half of the story. However, the docs frame parallelism as splitting work across projects or larger tasks, not as alternative attempts at one task, and nothing describes comparing attempts side by side or picking a winner. Missing for 10: documented multi-attempt (best-of-N) runs of the same task, a side-by-side comparison view, a select/merge-chosen-attempt workflow, and independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can run several task attempts in parallel and compare results before choosing one

citations.quote: Have multiple agents working in parallel, so larger tasks get tackled faster.
Orchestrate multiple autonomous agents working in parallel across independent projects.
Projects natively support Git worktrees, allowing agents to operate in isolated background folders.
